and Spatial Reasoning with LMM 6 7 [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2607.05493-b31b1b.svg?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05493) 8 [![ECCV 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/ECCV-2026-4b8bbe.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) 9 [![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Website-1e6cb6.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) 10 [![Dataset](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dataset-HuggingFace-fcd734.svg?logo=huggingface&logoColor=black)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset) 11 [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache--2.0-4caf50.svg)](LICENSE) 12 [![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-EE4C2C.svg?logo=pytorch&logoColor=white)](https://pytorch.org/) 13 14 --- 15 16 **Amol Harsh · Zongyan Han · Jean Lahoud · Ye Liu · Rao Muhammad Anwer · Hisham Cholakkal · Salman Khan · Fahad Shahbaz Khan** 17 18 **Ground3D-LMM** is a large multimodal model for **fine-grained 3D point grounding** and **spatial reasoning** in indoor scenes. It produces per-point segmentation masks alongside grounded natural-language answers across **8 sub-tasks** on ScanNet and ScanNet++, trained on a **2.47M Q/A pair** dataset. 19 20
21 22 --- 23 24 The architecture combines: 25 - **SpConvUNet** sparse 3D point encoder (from UniSeg3D) 26 - **Qwen3-VL-4B** vision-language model with LoRA fine-tuning 27 - **Mask2Former-style query decoder** (6 layers, 256-d) 28 - **Superpoint pooling** for efficient cross-attention over scenes 29 30 ## 📢 News 31 32 - **[Featured 📣]** *Ground3D-LMM* was featured by [52CV](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ZH2NctV9Ycg8t4EVui7gIg), a leading Chinese computer-vision community WeChat account. 33 - **[Accepted 🎉]** *Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM* accepted to **ECCV 2026** (main conference). 34 - **[Released]** Code and Ground3D dataset (2.47M Q/A pairs) released on Hugging Face. 35 36 ## 🏗️ Architecture 37 38 ![Ground3D-LMM architecture](images/method.png) 39 40 A 3D scene (XYZ + RGB point cloud) is encoded by **SpConvUNet** into per-point features, which are then pooled over precomputed superpoints to yield `Fp ∈ ℝ^(M × d)`. `Fp` is projected into two spaces in parallel: (i) into the **Qwen3-VL LMM** as `<|point|>` token embeddings alongside the text prompt and optional RGB frame, and (ii) into the **mask decoder** as keys/values for 6 layers of Mask2Former-style Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN. The LMM generates text that includes `` tokens; the hidden state at each `` becomes a refined query, which is dot-producted against per-point features to produce the final segmentation mask. 41 42 ## 🚀 Install 43 44 ```bash 45 conda create -n ground3d python=3.10 -y 46 conda activate ground3d 47 # Follow docs/INSTALL.md for the OpenMMLab stack + MinkowskiEngine (source builds), 48 # then install this package: 49 pip install -e . 50 ``` 51 52 > **Heads-up:** `conda env create -f environment.yml` does **not** fully work on its own — 53 > `mmcv==2.1.0` has no prebuilt wheel for torch 2.4.1 (needs a source build with an older 54 > `setuptools` + `--no-build-isolation`), and **MinkowskiEngine 0.5.4** must be compiled 55 > from source. Follow [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) **Option B** for the verified, 56 > step-by-step install, troubleshooting, and tested environment details. 57 58 **Tested**: Ubuntu 20.04 · Python 3.10 · PyTorch 2.4.1 · CUDA 11.8 · A100 80GB / RTX 3090. 59 60 ## ⚡ Quick Start with HuggingFace 61 62 ### Download the dataset 63 ```python 64 from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download 65 66 # Annotations only (~3 GB) for exploration 67 data_root = snapshot_download( 68 repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", 69 repo_type="dataset", 70 allow_patterns=["*/refined_qa_data/*", "*/part_ground3d_*.txt", "README.md"], 71 ) 72 73 # Full dataset (~150 GB) for training 74 # data_root = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset") 75 ``` 76 77 ### Download a pretrained checkpoint 78 ```python 79 from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download 80 81 # Joint variant — uses 3D point cloud + aligned RGB frames (main paper result) 82 ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint") 83 84 # Or the point-only variant — uses 3D points only (no RGB frames needed) 85 # ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D") 86 ``` 87 88 ### Run inference (single config-driven invocation) 89 90 Each released checkpoint has a matching eval config — the Joint (3D + 2D) variant uses 91 `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py` (LoRA r=16, RGB frames on), and the 3D-only variant 92 uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py` (LoRA r=32, no RGB frames). The `_3d` config 93 inherits from the joint one and only overrides those three fields. 94 95 ```bash 96 # --- Joint (3D + 2D) — main paper result --- 97 CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" 98 CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py 99 100 # --- Or, 3D-only --- 101 # CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" 102 # CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py 103 104 PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py \ 105 "$CONFIG" "$CKPT" \ 106 --work-dir work_dirs/quickstart \ 107 --cfg-options \ 108 "model.decoder.save_pred_qa_dir=work_dirs/quickstart/preds" \ 109 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_level=part_qa_data" \ 110 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_type=qa_data" \ 111 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.sub_task=scale_estimation" 112 ``` 113 114 This runs inference for the `scale_estimation` sub-task on `part_qa_data` and writes: 115 - Per-scene predictions to `work_dirs/quickstart/preds/{scene}.json` 116 - Segmentation mIoU to stdout 117 118 > For batched evaluation across sub-tasks or both datasets, `bash eval_ground3d.sh` auto-detects 119 > the variant from the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config — see the 120 > [Evaluation](#-evaluation) section. 121 122 ## 📊 Ground3D Dataset 123 124 Total **2,475,307 Q/A pairs** spanning 8 sub-tasks across ScanNet and ScanNet++ scenes. 125 126 | Source | Train scenes | Val scenes | Object QA | Part QA | Multi-turn | Total | 127 |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| 128 | ScanNet | 1,433 | 80 | 655,760 | 909,905 | 62,064 | 1,627,729 | 129 | ScanNet++ | 857 | 48 | 339,396 | 498,399 | 9,783 | 847,578 | 130 | **Total** | **2,290** | **128** | **995,156** | **1,408,304** | **71,847** | **2,475,307** | 131 132 > Not every ScanNet++ scene could be used: many scenes in the ScanNet++ release are missing the depth 133 > or mesh files our pipeline needs, and a few lost their Q/A during our VLM-based verification stage. 134 > The scene count here may therefore differ slightly from the paper, since some scenes were listed but 135 > held no Q/A and have been removed. **The total number of Q/A pairs is unchanged and matches the paper.** 136 137 ### Sub-tasks 138 1. `functional_part_grounding` 139 2. `functional_object_grounding` 140 3. `scale_estimation` 141 4. `grounded_dimension_reasoning` 142 5. `relative_depth_forward` 143 6. `existence_verification` 144 7. `scale_comparison_size` 145 8. `distance_estimation` 146 9. `relative_position_forward_reasoning` 147 148 Full dataset schema, Q/A JSON layout, and per-file specifications: see the [dataset card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset). 149 150 ### Prepare the data (download → convert) 151 152 **Step 1 — download** from Hugging Face. Each source (`scannet`, `scannetpp`) ships 153 the raw per-frame arrays plus QA JSON and split lists: 154 155 ``` 156 data/scannet/ 157 ├── processed_data//frame__vert.npy # XYZ+RGB points (load_dim=6) 158 │ frame__sp_label.npy # superpoint ids 159 │ frame__part_label.npy # per-point part labels 160 │ frame__object_label.npy # per-point object labels 161 ├── refined_qa_data/{part_qa,object_qa,multiturn_qa}//... 162 └── part_ground3d_{train,val}.txt # scene split lists 163 ``` 164 165 **Step 2 — convert** the raw `.npy` into the flat `.bin` files and the `infos.pkl` 166 the configs actually consume: 167 168 ```bash 169 python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ 170 --root-path data/scannet \ 171 --out-dir data/scannet \ 172 --qa_data_dir data/scannet/refined_qa_data 173 ``` 174 175 **ScanNet++** uses the identical layout — just swap the paths (the converter is dataset-agnostic; 176 the ScanNet++ config reuses `data/scannet/scannet_cls_embedding.pth`): 177 178 ```bash 179 python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ 180 --root-path data/scannetpp \ 181 --out-dir data/scannetpp \ 182 --qa_data_dir data/scannetpp/refined_qa_data 183 ``` 184 185 Resulting layout (what the configs load via `ann_file` + `data_prefix`): 186 187 ``` 188 data/scannet/ 189 ├── points/ super_points/ part_mask/ object_mask/ (_frame_.bin) 190 ├── part3d_glamm_infos_train.pkl 191 ├── part3d_glamm_infos_val.pkl 192 └── scannet_cls_embedding.pth (shipped in this repo) 193 ``` 194 195 > **Joint model only:** the config's `model.decoder.image_dir` expects RGB frames at 196 > `data/scannet/frame_images//.jpg`. These are ScanNet / ScanNet++ images and are 197 > **not redistributable** (so they are not on Hugging Face). Download the raw datasets and extract 198 > the frames each split needs by following **[docs/DATA_IMAGES.md](docs/DATA_IMAGES.md)** 199 > (`tools/build_frame_images.py` does it straight from the `.pkl`). Or use the **3D-only** 200 > checkpoint, which needs no images (`model.decoder.image_dir=None`). 201 202 ## 🤗 Model Zoo 203 204 | Model | Modality | LoRA (r / α) | Eval config | Checkpoint | 205 |---|---|---|---|---| 206 | Ground3D-LMM-4B (Joint) | 3D points + RGB frames | 16 / 32 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint) — main paper result | 207 | Ground3D-LMM-4B (3D-only) | 3D points only | 32 / 64 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}_3d.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D) — no RGB frames required | 208 209 Both checkpoints use **Qwen3-VL-4B** as the LLM backbone (4.47B params, ~400M LoRA-trainable). 210 The two variants have different LoRA ranks, so each ships with its own eval config; the config 211 inheritance keeps the diff between them tiny (`lora_r`, `lora_alpha`, `image_dir`). If you're 212 running through `eval_ground3d.sh`, the launcher probes the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks 213 the matching config automatically — no manual switch needed. 214 215 ## 🏋️ Training 216 217 ### Prepare data 218 1. Download the dataset and arrange under `data/scannet/` and `data/scannetpp/` (see [Local data layout](#local-data-layout)) 219 2. Download pretrained sparse-conv weights into `work_dirs/pretrained/`: 220 - `sstnet_scannet.pth` — used as the point-encoder initialization 221 3. The Qwen3-VL-4B base model will be downloaded automatically by `transformers`. To use a local copy, override via `--cfg-options model.decoder.qwen_model_path=/path/to/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` 222 223 ### Launch training (4 GPUs, LoRA fine-tuning) 224 ```bash 225 bash train.sh 226 ``` 227 228 This launches `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py` on GPUs 0-3 via `torch.distributed.launch`. Checkpoints are saved to `work_dirs/ground3dlmm/epoch_*.pth`. 229 230 ### Customize the training run 231 Common arguments to edit in `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py`: 232 233 | Field | Default | Purpose | 234 |---|---|---| 235 | `model.decoder.qwen_model_path` | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` | Path or HF id of the LLM | 236 | `model.decoder.lora_r`, `lora_alpha` | 16, 32 | LoRA rank and scaling | 237 | `model.decoder.max_point_tokens` | 2000 | Max superpoint tokens fed to LLM | 238 | `train_dataloader.batch_size` | 1 | Per-GPU batch size | 239 | `optim_wrapper.optimizer.lr` | 1e-4 | Base learning rate | 240 | `epoch` | 10 | Total training epochs | 241 | `load_from` | `work_dirs/pretrained/sstnet_scannet.pth` | Backbone init | 242 243 ## 📈 Evaluation 244 245 The paper reports **three categories of metrics**. Full evaluation is a 3-step pipeline: 246 247 ### Step 1 — Run inference (segmentation mIoU + per-scene predictions) 248 249 One launcher, fully argument-driven — pick the dataset / task levels / sub-tasks with flags: 250 ```bash 251 bash eval_ground3d.sh --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # default: scannet, part+object, all sub-tasks 252 253 # choose exactly what to run: 254 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels all # both datasets, part+object+multi_turn 255 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannet --levels part,object --sub_tasks distance_estimation,scale_estimation 256 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannetpp --levels multi_turn 257 bash eval_ground3d.sh --help # full option list (+ --gpus, --out-root, --mask-dump) 258 ``` 259 `--dataset` = `scannet`|`scannetpp`|`all`; `--levels` = any of `part,object,multi_turn` (or `all`); 260 `--sub_tasks` = `all` or a comma list. `--variant` = `joint`|`3d`|`auto` (default `auto`): the launcher 261 inspects the checkpoint's LoRA rank (`r=16` → joint, `r=32` → 3D-only) and picks the matching config, 262 so the Joint and 3D-only weights just work with the same command. Pass `--variant` explicitly to 263 override. The old names `eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp,all}.sh` still work — they're thin wrappers 264 that pass flags through. Outputs: 265 - **Segmentation mIoU** (printed per sub-task) 266 - Per-scene prediction JSONs in `val_outputs_joint/{scannet,scannetpp}/pred_qa_data_val/...` 267 268 > Add `--mask-dump ` to also dump per-QA masks (needed for the **GM-δ** stage below, and used by 269 > the grounding visualization). 270 271 `tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py` runs **two independent stages** — pick what you need via `--stages` 272 (`ape`, `judge`, or `all`). The `--input` dir is searched **recursively**, nested / multi-turn 273 prediction JSONs are flattened automatically, and each sample is tagged with its task. `ape` uses a 274 text LLM (`--llm_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`) to extract numbers; `judge` uses 275 the paper's VL judge (`--judge_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`). Both run via 276 **HuggingFace transformers**. Sanity-check the numeric math with 277 `python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --selftest`. 278 279 ### Step 2 — `ape` : numeric APE + δ@1.25 (the 4 numeric tasks only) 280 ```bash 281 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ 282 --output eval_results/scannet_ape.json --stages ape \ 283 --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 284 ``` 285 Runs **only** on `distance_estimation`, `grounded_dimension_reasoning`, `scale_estimation`, 286 `scale_comparison_size`. The LLM extracts the scalar(s) in metres (per-task JSON shape; a missing 287 prediction → `0.0` so it is penalised), then reports **APE** `|ŝ−s|/s×100%` and **δ@1.25** success 288 (`δ = max(ŝ/s, s/ŝ) ≤ 1.25`; GT==0 pairs skipped; mean over pairs, then macro-averaged per task). 289 290 ### Step 3 — `judge` : LLM judge — Hallucination + Completeness (all tasks) 291 ```bash 292 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ 293 --output eval_results/scannet_judge.json --stages judge \ 294 --judge_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct --gpus 0,1,2,3 295 ``` 296 The Table-4 judge — **Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct** — scores each prediction and reports **Hallucination** 297 and **Completeness** (over all tasks). Run both stages with `--stages all` (the `ape` extractor 298 stays on the text `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`). 299 300 ### Step 3b — `gmdelta` : GM-δ (supplementary, opt-in) 301 GM-δ (Grounded-Measurement) counts a prediction correct only when **mask IoU > 0.3 AND δ ≤ 1.25**, on 302 the numeric tasks that also ground. Run the numeric sub-tasks **with `--mask-dump`** (the mask tree 303 mirrors the prediction tree), then **one command auto-iterates all 4 numeric tasks × both datasets**: 304 ```bash 305 # 1. inference for the 4 numeric tasks on both datasets, dumping per-QA masks 306 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels part \ 307 --sub_tasks distance_estimation,grounded_dimension_reasoning,scale_estimation,scale_comparison_size \ 308 --mask-dump masks --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth 309 310 # 2. GM-δ across all of them in a single run 311 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta \ 312 --input val_outputs_joint --mask_dump_dir masks \ 313 --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 --output eval_results/gmdelta.json 314 ``` 315 It reports GM-δ **per (dataset, task)** and **overall**. `--gmdelta_task all` (default) auto-discovers 316 the numeric tasks; pass a single task name to restrict. 317 318 ### Metric provenance (the paper's metrics) 319 320 | Metric | Provided by | Tasks | 321 |---|---|---| 322 | Segmentation mIoU | `tools/test.py` → `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` | all sub-tasks (over each QA's `` grounding) | 323 | APE & δ@1.25 (LLM-extracted) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages ape` | 4 numeric tasks | 324 | Hallucination + Completeness (LLM judge) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages judge` | all tasks | 325 | GM-δ (IoU>0.3 ∧ δ≤1.25), *supplementary* | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta` | grounded-measurement | 326 327 > mIoU is computed per `(level, sub-task)` over the QAs that emit a `` grounding. Every sub-task 328 > grounds, so all of them get a mIoU — the only partial case is `existence_verification`, where the 329 > pure yes/no answers carry no mask and are simply excluded from its mIoU. 330 331 ## 🔁 ScanRefer & Reason3D (Tables 5–6) 332 333 Ground3D-LMM is also fine-tuned + evaluated on the ScanRefer and Reason3D referring/reasoning 334 benchmarks, in both **3D** and **3D+2D** (point cloud + the scene's 20 RGB views) settings: 335 336 | Row | Config | Checkpoint | mIoU | 337 |---|---|---|---| 338 | ScanRefer 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-3D` | 38.72 | 339 | ScanRefer 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-Joint` | 41.30 | 340 | Reason3D 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-3D` | 36.35 | 341 | Reason3D 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-Joint` | 41.29 | 342 343 Data prep (annotations → `*_infos.pkl` via `tools/create_data_{scanrefer,reason3d}.py`, and the 344 20-view images via `tools/build_scene_images.py`) and the eval commands are in 345 **[docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md](docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md)**. 346 347 ## 🎨 Grounding visualization 348 349 Color the model's predicted `` masks on the scene point cloud and save a `.ply` 350 (1 `` → red, 2 → red + green, N → palette). Two steps: 351 352 ```bash 353 # 1. dump predicted masks during inference (toggle on, via config or env) 354 PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py "$CKPT" \ 355 --cfg-options model.decoder.save_viz_dir=viz_dumps ... # (or: MASK_DUMP_DIR=viz_dumps bash eval_ground3d_scannet.sh) 356 357 # 2. turn the dumps into colored point clouds (offline, no GPU/Open3D) 358 python tools/export_grounding_ply.py \ 359 --masks_dir viz_dumps --points_dir data/scannet/points --out viz_ply 360 ``` 361 362 `--mode combine` (default) writes one `.ply` per scene/conversation, coloring each grounded region 363 red, green, ...; `--mode per_qa` writes one red-masked `.ply` per question. Core writer: 364 `uniseg3d/grounding_viz.py`. For multi-turn dialogues (`task_level=multi_turn_qa_data`) each grounding 365 turn contributes one region, so a cross-object conversation produces one red object and one green 366 object in a single `.ply`. 367 368 ## 🛠️ Repository structure 369 370 ``` 371 Ground3D-LMM/ 372 ├── configs/ 373 │ ├── ground3dlmm_train.py 374 │ ├── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py 375 │ └── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannetpp.py 376 ├── data/ (user-populated; see Local data layout) 377 ├── docs/ 378 │ └── INSTALL.md 379 ├── tools/ 380 │ ├── train.py, test.py 381 │ ├── dist_train.sh, dist_test.sh 382 │ ├── create_data.py 383 │ └── evaluate_text_metrics.py 384 ├── uniseg3d/ (model + transforms + criteria) 385 │ ├── uniseg3d.py Grounded_LMM_main (entry point) 386 │ ├── query_decoder.py Grounded_Decoder_Joint / _Eval 387 │ ├── spconv_unet.py point encoder 388 │ ├── point_qwen3_vl.py Qwen3-VL with point-embedding injection 389 │ ├── transforms_3d.py QA_Generation_v2 / _Test 390 │ ├── unified_metric.py Part3DGlamm_SegMetric 391 │ └── ... 392 ├── work_dirs/ (checkpoints + logs, gitignored) 393 ├── train.sh one-line training launcher 394 ├── eval_ground3d_scannet.sh eval on ScanNet 395 ├── eval_ground3d_scannetpp.sh eval on ScanNet++ 396 ├── eval_ground3d_all.sh eval on both 397 ├── environment.yml conda spec (pinned versions) 398 ├── pyproject.toml 399 └── LICENSE Apache-2.0 400 ``` 401 402 ## 🙏 Acknowledgments 403 404 This codebase builds upon several open-source projects: 405 406 - **[UniSeg3D](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D)** — sparse 3D point encoder + Mask2Former-style decoder 407 - **[Qwen3-VL](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL)** — vision-language model backbone 408 - **[mmdetection3d](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d)** — 3D data pipeline and registry framework 409 - **[Mask2Former](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former)** — masked-attention decoder design 410 411 ## 📚 Citation 412 413 If you find Ground3D-LMM useful for your research, please cite: 414 415 ```bibtex 416 @inproceedings{ground3dlmm2026, 417 title = {Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding 418 and Spatial Reasoning with LMM}, 419 author = {Harsh, Amol and Han, Zongyan and Lahoud, Jean 420 and Liu, Ye and Anwer, Rao Muhammad 421 and Cholakkal, Hisham and Khan, Salman 422 and Khan, Fahad Shahbaz}, 423 booktitle = {Proceedings of the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)}, 424 year = {2026}, 425 eprint = {2607.05493}, 426 archivePrefix = {arXiv}, 427 primaryClass = {cs.CV} 428 } 429 ``` 430 431 ## 📄 License 432 433 Released under the [Apache 2.0 License](LICENSE). 434

# Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding
and Spatial Reasoning with LMM [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2607.05493-b31b1b.svg?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05493) [![ECCV 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/ECCV-2026-4b8bbe.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) [![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Website-1e6cb6.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) [![Dataset](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dataset-HuggingFace-fcd734.svg?logo=huggingface&logoColor=black)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache--2.0-4caf50.svg)](LICENSE) [![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-EE4C2C.svg?logo=pytorch&logoColor=white)](https://pytorch.org/) --- **Amol Harsh · Zongyan Han · Jean Lahoud · Ye Liu · Rao Muhammad Anwer · Hisham Cholakkal · Salman Khan · Fahad Shahbaz Khan** **Ground3D-LMM** is a large multimodal model for **fine-grained 3D point grounding** and **spatial reasoning** in indoor scenes. It produces per-point segmentation masks alongside grounded natural-language answers across **8 sub-tasks** on ScanNet and ScanNet++, trained on a **2.47M Q/A pair** dataset.
--- The architecture combines: - **SpConvUNet** sparse 3D point encoder (from UniSeg3D) - **Qwen3-VL-4B** vision-language model with LoRA fine-tuning - **Mask2Former-style query decoder** (6 layers, 256-d) - **Superpoint pooling** for efficient cross-attention over scenes ## 📢 News - **[Featured 📣]** *Ground3D-LMM* was featured by [52CV](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ZH2NctV9Ycg8t4EVui7gIg), a leading Chinese computer-vision community WeChat account. - **[Accepted 🎉]** *Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM* accepted to **ECCV 2026** (main conference). - **[Released]** Code and Ground3D dataset (2.47M Q/A pairs) released on Hugging Face. ## 🏗️ Architecture ![Ground3D-LMM architecture](images/method.png) A 3D scene (XYZ + RGB point cloud) is encoded by **SpConvUNet** into per-point features, which are then pooled over precomputed superpoints to yield `Fp ∈ ℝ^(M × d)`. `Fp` is projected into two spaces in parallel: (i) into the **Qwen3-VL LMM** as `<|point|>` token embeddings alongside the text prompt and optional RGB frame, and (ii) into the **mask decoder** as keys/values for 6 layers of Mask2Former-style Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN. The LMM generates text that includes `` tokens; the hidden state at each `` becomes a refined query, which is dot-producted against per-point features to produce the final segmentation mask. ## 🚀 Install ```bash conda create -n ground3d python=3.10 -y conda activate ground3d # Follow docs/INSTALL.md for the OpenMMLab stack + MinkowskiEngine (source builds), # then install this package: pip install -e . ``` > **Heads-up:** `conda env create -f environment.yml` does **not** fully work on its own — > `mmcv==2.1.0` has no prebuilt wheel for torch 2.4.1 (needs a source build with an older > `setuptools` + `--no-build-isolation`), and **MinkowskiEngine 0.5.4** must be compiled > from source. Follow [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) **Option B** for the verified, > step-by-step install, troubleshooting, and tested environment details. **Tested**: Ubuntu 20.04 · Python 3.10 · PyTorch 2.4.1 · CUDA 11.8 · A100 80GB / RTX 3090. ## ⚡ Quick Start with HuggingFace ### Download the dataset ```python from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download # Annotations only (~3 GB) for exploration data_root = snapshot_download( repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset", allow_patterns=["*/refined_qa_data/*", "*/part_ground3d_*.txt", "README.md"], ) # Full dataset (~150 GB) for training # data_root = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset") ``` ### Download a pretrained checkpoint ```python from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download # Joint variant — uses 3D point cloud + aligned RGB frames (main paper result) ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint") # Or the point-only variant — uses 3D points only (no RGB frames needed) # ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D") ``` ### Run inference (single config-driven invocation) Each released checkpoint has a matching eval config — the Joint (3D + 2D) variant uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py` (LoRA r=16, RGB frames on), and the 3D-only variant uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py` (LoRA r=32, no RGB frames). The `_3d` config inherits from the joint one and only overrides those three fields. ```bash # --- Joint (3D + 2D) — main paper result --- CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py # --- Or, 3D-only --- # CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" # CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py \ "$CONFIG" "$CKPT" \ --work-dir work_dirs/quickstart \ --cfg-options \ "model.decoder.save_pred_qa_dir=work_dirs/quickstart/preds" \ "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_level=part_qa_data" \ "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_type=qa_data" \ "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.sub_task=scale_estimation" ``` This runs inference for the `scale_estimation` sub-task on `part_qa_data` and writes: - Per-scene predictions to `work_dirs/quickstart/preds/{scene}.json` - Segmentation mIoU to stdout > For batched evaluation across sub-tasks or both datasets, `bash eval_ground3d.sh` auto-detects > the variant from the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config — see the > [Evaluation](#-evaluation) section. ## 📊 Ground3D Dataset Total **2,475,307 Q/A pairs** spanning 8 sub-tasks across ScanNet and ScanNet++ scenes. | Source | Train scenes | Val scenes | Object QA | Part QA | Multi-turn | Total | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | ScanNet | 1,433 | 80 | 655,760 | 909,905 | 62,064 | 1,627,729 | | ScanNet++ | 857 | 48 | 339,396 | 498,399 | 9,783 | 847,578 | | **Total** | **2,290** | **128** | **995,156** | **1,408,304** | **71,847** | **2,475,307** | > Not every ScanNet++ scene could be used: many scenes in the ScanNet++ release are missing the depth > or mesh files our pipeline needs, and a few lost their Q/A during our VLM-based verification stage. > The scene count here may therefore differ slightly from the paper, since some scenes were listed but > held no Q/A and have been removed. **The total number of Q/A pairs is unchanged and matches the paper.** ### Sub-tasks 1. `functional_part_grounding` 2. `functional_object_grounding` 3. `scale_estimation` 4. `grounded_dimension_reasoning` 5. `relative_depth_forward` 6. `existence_verification` 7. `scale_comparison_size` 8. `distance_estimation` 9. `relative_position_forward_reasoning` Full dataset schema, Q/A JSON layout, and per-file specifications: see the [dataset card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset). ### Prepare the data (download → convert) **Step 1 — download** from Hugging Face. Each source (`scannet`, `scannetpp`) ships the raw per-frame arrays plus QA JSON and split lists: ``` data/scannet/ ├── processed_data//frame__vert.npy # XYZ+RGB points (load_dim=6) │ frame__sp_label.npy # superpoint ids │ frame__part_label.npy # per-point part labels │ frame__object_label.npy # per-point object labels ├── refined_qa_data/{part_qa,object_qa,multiturn_qa}//... └── part_ground3d_{train,val}.txt # scene split lists ``` **Step 2 — convert** the raw `.npy` into the flat `.bin` files and the `infos.pkl` the configs actually consume: ```bash python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ --root-path data/scannet \ --out-dir data/scannet \ --qa_data_dir data/scannet/refined_qa_data ``` **ScanNet++** uses the identical layout — just swap the paths (the converter is dataset-agnostic; the ScanNet++ config reuses `data/scannet/scannet_cls_embedding.pth`): ```bash python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ --root-path data/scannetpp \ --out-dir data/scannetpp \ --qa_data_dir data/scannetpp/refined_qa_data ``` Resulting layout (what the configs load via `ann_file` + `data_prefix`): ``` data/scannet/ ├── points/ super_points/ part_mask/ object_mask/ (_frame_.bin) ├── part3d_glamm_infos_train.pkl ├── part3d_glamm_infos_val.pkl └── scannet_cls_embedding.pth (shipped in this repo) ``` > **Joint model only:** the config's `model.decoder.image_dir` expects RGB frames at > `data/scannet/frame_images//.jpg`. These are ScanNet / ScanNet++ images and are > **not redistributable** (so they are not on Hugging Face). Download the raw datasets and extract > the frames each split needs by following **[docs/DATA_IMAGES.md](docs/DATA_IMAGES.md)** > (`tools/build_frame_images.py` does it straight from the `.pkl`). Or use the **3D-only** > checkpoint, which needs no images (`model.decoder.image_dir=None`). ## 🤗 Model Zoo | Model | Modality | LoRA (r / α) | Eval config | Checkpoint | |---|---|---|---|---| | Ground3D-LMM-4B (Joint) | 3D points + RGB frames | 16 / 32 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint) — main paper result | | Ground3D-LMM-4B (3D-only) | 3D points only | 32 / 64 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}_3d.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D) — no RGB frames required | Both checkpoints use **Qwen3-VL-4B** as the LLM backbone (4.47B params, ~400M LoRA-trainable). The two variants have different LoRA ranks, so each ships with its own eval config; the config inheritance keeps the diff between them tiny (`lora_r`, `lora_alpha`, `image_dir`). If you're running through `eval_ground3d.sh`, the launcher probes the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config automatically — no manual switch needed. ## 🏋️ Training ### Prepare data 1. Download the dataset and arrange under `data/scannet/` and `data/scannetpp/` (see [Local data layout](#local-data-layout)) 2. Download pretrained sparse-conv weights into `work_dirs/pretrained/`: - `sstnet_scannet.pth` — used as the point-encoder initialization 3. The Qwen3-VL-4B base model will be downloaded automatically by `transformers`. To use a local copy, override via `--cfg-options model.decoder.qwen_model_path=/path/to/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` ### Launch training (4 GPUs, LoRA fine-tuning) ```bash bash train.sh ``` This launches `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py` on GPUs 0-3 via `torch.distributed.launch`. Checkpoints are saved to `work_dirs/ground3dlmm/epoch_*.pth`. ### Customize the training run Common arguments to edit in `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py`: | Field | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `model.decoder.qwen_model_path` | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` | Path or HF id of the LLM | | `model.decoder.lora_r`, `lora_alpha` | 16, 32 | LoRA rank and scaling | | `model.decoder.max_point_tokens` | 2000 | Max superpoint tokens fed to LLM | | `train_dataloader.batch_size` | 1 | Per-GPU batch size | | `optim_wrapper.optimizer.lr` | 1e-4 | Base learning rate | | `epoch` | 10 | Total training epochs | | `load_from` | `work_dirs/pretrained/sstnet_scannet.pth` | Backbone init | ## 📈 Evaluation The paper reports **three categories of metrics**. Full evaluation is a 3-step pipeline: ### Step 1 — Run inference (segmentation mIoU + per-scene predictions) One launcher, fully argument-driven — pick the dataset / task levels / sub-tasks with flags: ```bash bash eval_ground3d.sh --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # default: scannet, part+object, all sub-tasks # choose exactly what to run: bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels all # both datasets, part+object+multi_turn bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannet --levels part,object --sub_tasks distance_estimation,scale_estimation bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannetpp --levels multi_turn bash eval_ground3d.sh --help # full option list (+ --gpus, --out-root, --mask-dump) ``` `--dataset` = `scannet`|`scannetpp`|`all`; `--levels` = any of `part,object,multi_turn` (or `all`); `--sub_tasks` = `all` or a comma list. `--variant` = `joint`|`3d`|`auto` (default `auto`): the launcher inspects the checkpoint's LoRA rank (`r=16` → joint, `r=32` → 3D-only) and picks the matching config, so the Joint and 3D-only weights just work with the same command. Pass `--variant` explicitly to override. The old names `eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp,all}.sh` still work — they're thin wrappers that pass flags through. Outputs: - **Segmentation mIoU** (printed per sub-task) - Per-scene prediction JSONs in `val_outputs_joint/{scannet,scannetpp}/pred_qa_data_val/...` > Add `--mask-dump ` to also dump per-QA masks (needed for the **GM-δ** stage below, and used by > the grounding visualization). `tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py` runs **two independent stages** — pick what you need via `--stages` (`ape`, `judge`, or `all`). The `--input` dir is searched **recursively**, nested / multi-turn prediction JSONs are flattened automatically, and each sample is tagged with its task. `ape` uses a text LLM (`--llm_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`) to extract numbers; `judge` uses the paper's VL judge (`--judge_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`). Both run via **HuggingFace transformers**. Sanity-check the numeric math with `python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --selftest`. ### Step 2 — `ape` : numeric APE + δ@1.25 (the 4 numeric tasks only) ```bash python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ --output eval_results/scannet_ape.json --stages ape \ --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 ``` Runs **only** on `distance_estimation`, `grounded_dimension_reasoning`, `scale_estimation`, `scale_comparison_size`. The LLM extracts the scalar(s) in metres (per-task JSON shape; a missing prediction → `0.0` so it is penalised), then reports **APE** `|ŝ−s|/s×100%` and **δ@1.25** success (`δ = max(ŝ/s, s/ŝ) ≤ 1.25`; GT==0 pairs skipped; mean over pairs, then macro-averaged per task). ### Step 3 — `judge` : LLM judge — Hallucination + Completeness (all tasks) ```bash python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ --output eval_results/scannet_judge.json --stages judge \ --judge_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct --gpus 0,1,2,3 ``` The Table-4 judge — **Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct** — scores each prediction and reports **Hallucination** and **Completeness** (over all tasks). Run both stages with `--stages all` (the `ape` extractor stays on the text `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`). ### Step 3b — `gmdelta` : GM-δ (supplementary, opt-in) GM-δ (Grounded-Measurement) counts a prediction correct only when **mask IoU > 0.3 AND δ ≤ 1.25**, on the numeric tasks that also ground. Run the numeric sub-tasks **with `--mask-dump`** (the mask tree mirrors the prediction tree), then **one command auto-iterates all 4 numeric tasks × both datasets**: ```bash # 1. inference for the 4 numeric tasks on both datasets, dumping per-QA masks bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels part \ --sub_tasks distance_estimation,grounded_dimension_reasoning,scale_estimation,scale_comparison_size \ --mask-dump masks --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # 2. GM-δ across all of them in a single run python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta \ --input val_outputs_joint --mask_dump_dir masks \ --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 --output eval_results/gmdelta.json ``` It reports GM-δ **per (dataset, task)** and **overall**. `--gmdelta_task all` (default) auto-discovers the numeric tasks; pass a single task name to restrict. ### Metric provenance (the paper's metrics) | Metric | Provided by | Tasks | |---|---|---| | Segmentation mIoU | `tools/test.py` → `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` | all sub-tasks (over each QA's `` grounding) | | APE & δ@1.25 (LLM-extracted) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages ape` | 4 numeric tasks | | Hallucination + Completeness (LLM judge) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages judge` | all tasks | | GM-δ (IoU>0.3 ∧ δ≤1.25), *supplementary* | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta` | grounded-measurement | > mIoU is computed per `(level, sub-task)` over the QAs that emit a `` grounding. Every sub-task > grounds, so all of them get a mIoU — the only partial case is `existence_verification`, where the > pure yes/no answers carry no mask and are simply excluded from its mIoU. ## 🔁 ScanRefer & Reason3D (Tables 5–6) Ground3D-LMM is also fine-tuned + evaluated on the ScanRefer and Reason3D referring/reasoning benchmarks, in both **3D** and **3D+2D** (point cloud + the scene's 20 RGB views) settings: | Row | Config | Checkpoint | mIoU | |---|---|---|---| | ScanRefer 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-3D` | 38.72 | | ScanRefer 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-Joint` | 41.30 | | Reason3D 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-3D` | 36.35 | | Reason3D 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-Joint` | 41.29 | Data prep (annotations → `*_infos.pkl` via `tools/create_data_{scanrefer,reason3d}.py`, and the 20-view images via `tools/build_scene_images.py`) and the eval commands are in **[docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md](docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md)**. ## 🎨 Grounding visualization Color the model's predicted `` masks on the scene point cloud and save a `.ply` (1 `` → red, 2 → red + green, N → palette). Two steps: ```bash # 1. dump predicted masks during inference (toggle on, via config or env) PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py "$CKPT" \ --cfg-options model.decoder.save_viz_dir=viz_dumps ... # (or: MASK_DUMP_DIR=viz_dumps bash eval_ground3d_scannet.sh) # 2. turn the dumps into colored point clouds (offline, no GPU/Open3D) python tools/export_grounding_ply.py \ --masks_dir viz_dumps --points_dir data/scannet/points --out viz_ply ``` `--mode combine` (default) writes one `.ply` per scene/conversation, coloring each grounded region red, green, ...; `--mode per_qa` writes one red-masked `.ply` per question. Core writer: `uniseg3d/grounding_viz.py`. For multi-turn dialogues (`task_level=multi_turn_qa_data`) each grounding turn contributes one region, so a cross-object conversation produces one red object and one green object in a single `.ply`. ## 🛠️ Repository structure ``` Ground3D-LMM/ ├── configs/ │ ├── ground3dlmm_train.py │ ├── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py │ └── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannetpp.py ├── data/ (user-populated; see Local data layout) ├── docs/ │ └── INSTALL.md ├── tools/ │ ├── train.py, test.py │ ├── dist_train.sh, dist_test.sh │ ├── create_data.py │ └── evaluate_text_metrics.py ├── uniseg3d/ (model + transforms + criteria) │ ├── uniseg3d.py Grounded_LMM_main (entry point) │ ├── query_decoder.py Grounded_Decoder_Joint / _Eval │ ├── spconv_unet.py point encoder │ ├── point_qwen3_vl.py Qwen3-VL with point-embedding injection │ ├── transforms_3d.py QA_Generation_v2 / _Test │ ├── unified_metric.py Part3DGlamm_SegMetric │ └── ... ├── work_dirs/ (checkpoints + logs, gitignored) ├── train.sh one-line training launcher ├── eval_ground3d_scannet.sh eval on ScanNet ├── eval_ground3d_scannetpp.sh eval on ScanNet++ ├── eval_ground3d_all.sh eval on both ├── environment.yml conda spec (pinned versions) ├── pyproject.toml └── LICENSE Apache-2.0 ``` ## 🙏 Acknowledgments This codebase builds upon several open-source projects: - **[UniSeg3D](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D)** — sparse 3D point encoder + Mask2Former-style decoder - **[Qwen3-VL](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL)** — vision-language model backbone - **[mmdetection3d](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d)** — 3D data pipeline and registry framework - **[Mask2Former](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former)** — masked-attention decoder design ## 📚 Citation If you find Ground3D-LMM useful for your research, please cite: ```bibtex @inproceedings{ground3dlmm2026, title = {Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM}, author = {Harsh, Amol and Han, Zongyan and Lahoud, Jean and Liu, Ye and Anwer, Rao Muhammad and Cholakkal, Hisham and Khan, Salman and Khan, Fahad Shahbaz}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)}, year = {2026}, eprint = {2607.05493}, archivePrefix = {arXiv}, primaryClass = {cs.CV} } ``` ## 📄 License Released under the [Apache 2.0 License](LICENSE).

21 22 --- 23 24 The architecture combines: 25 - **SpConvUNet** sparse 3D point encoder (from UniSeg3D) 26 - **Qwen3-VL-4B** vision-language model with LoRA fine-tuning 27 - **Mask2Former-style query decoder** (6 layers, 256-d) 28 - **Superpoint pooling** for efficient cross-attention over scenes 29 30 ## 📢 News 31 32 - **[Featured 📣]** *Ground3D-LMM* was featured by [52CV](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ZH2NctV9Ycg8t4EVui7gIg), a leading Chinese computer-vision community WeChat account. 33 - **[Accepted 🎉]** *Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM* accepted to **ECCV 2026** (main conference). 34 - **[Released]** Code and Ground3D dataset (2.47M Q/A pairs) released on Hugging Face. 35 36 ## 🏗️ Architecture 37 38 ![Ground3D-LMM architecture](images/method.png) 39 40 A 3D scene (XYZ + RGB point cloud) is encoded by **SpConvUNet** into per-point features, which are then pooled over precomputed superpoints to yield `Fp ∈ ℝ^(M × d)`. `Fp` is projected into two spaces in parallel: (i) into the **Qwen3-VL LMM** as `<|point|>` token embeddings alongside the text prompt and optional RGB frame, and (ii) into the **mask decoder** as keys/values for 6 layers of Mask2Former-style Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN. The LMM generates text that includes `` tokens; the hidden state at each `` becomes a refined query, which is dot-producted against per-point features to produce the final segmentation mask. 41 42 ## 🚀 Install 43 44 ```bash 45 conda create -n ground3d python=3.10 -y 46 conda activate ground3d 47 # Follow docs/INSTALL.md for the OpenMMLab stack + MinkowskiEngine (source builds), 48 # then install this package: 49 pip install -e . 50 ``` 51 52 > **Heads-up:** `conda env create -f environment.yml` does **not** fully work on its own — 53 > `mmcv==2.1.0` has no prebuilt wheel for torch 2.4.1 (needs a source build with an older 54 > `setuptools` + `--no-build-isolation`), and **MinkowskiEngine 0.5.4** must be compiled 55 > from source. Follow [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) **Option B** for the verified, 56 > step-by-step install, troubleshooting, and tested environment details. 57 58 **Tested**: Ubuntu 20.04 · Python 3.10 · PyTorch 2.4.1 · CUDA 11.8 · A100 80GB / RTX 3090. 59 60 ## ⚡ Quick Start with HuggingFace 61 62 ### Download the dataset 63 ```python 64 from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download 65 66 # Annotations only (~3 GB) for exploration 67 data_root = snapshot_download( 68 repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", 69 repo_type="dataset", 70 allow_patterns=["*/refined_qa_data/*", "*/part_ground3d_*.txt", "README.md"], 71 ) 72 73 # Full dataset (~150 GB) for training 74 # data_root = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset") 75 ``` 76 77 ### Download a pretrained checkpoint 78 ```python 79 from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download 80 81 # Joint variant — uses 3D point cloud + aligned RGB frames (main paper result) 82 ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint") 83 84 # Or the point-only variant — uses 3D points only (no RGB frames needed) 85 # ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D") 86 ``` 87 88 ### Run inference (single config-driven invocation) 89 90 Each released checkpoint has a matching eval config — the Joint (3D + 2D) variant uses 91 `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py` (LoRA r=16, RGB frames on), and the 3D-only variant 92 uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py` (LoRA r=32, no RGB frames). The `_3d` config 93 inherits from the joint one and only overrides those three fields. 94 95 ```bash 96 # --- Joint (3D + 2D) — main paper result --- 97 CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" 98 CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py 99 100 # --- Or, 3D-only --- 101 # CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" 102 # CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py 103 104 PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py \ 105 "$CONFIG" "$CKPT" \ 106 --work-dir work_dirs/quickstart \ 107 --cfg-options \ 108 "model.decoder.save_pred_qa_dir=work_dirs/quickstart/preds" \ 109 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_level=part_qa_data" \ 110 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_type=qa_data" \ 111 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.sub_task=scale_estimation" 112 ``` 113 114 This runs inference for the `scale_estimation` sub-task on `part_qa_data` and writes: 115 - Per-scene predictions to `work_dirs/quickstart/preds/{scene}.json` 116 - Segmentation mIoU to stdout 117 118 > For batched evaluation across sub-tasks or both datasets, `bash eval_ground3d.sh` auto-detects 119 > the variant from the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config — see the 120 > [Evaluation](#-evaluation) section. 121 122 ## 📊 Ground3D Dataset 123 124 Total **2,475,307 Q/A pairs** spanning 8 sub-tasks across ScanNet and ScanNet++ scenes. 125 126 | Source | Train scenes | Val scenes | Object QA | Part QA | Multi-turn | Total | 127 |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| 128 | ScanNet | 1,433 | 80 | 655,760 | 909,905 | 62,064 | 1,627,729 | 129 | ScanNet++ | 857 | 48 | 339,396 | 498,399 | 9,783 | 847,578 | 130 | **Total** | **2,290** | **128** | **995,156** | **1,408,304** | **71,847** | **2,475,307** | 131 132 > Not every ScanNet++ scene could be used: many scenes in the ScanNet++ release are missing the depth 133 > or mesh files our pipeline needs, and a few lost their Q/A during our VLM-based verification stage. 134 > The scene count here may therefore differ slightly from the paper, since some scenes were listed but 135 > held no Q/A and have been removed. **The total number of Q/A pairs is unchanged and matches the paper.** 136 137 ### Sub-tasks 138 1. `functional_part_grounding` 139 2. `functional_object_grounding` 140 3. `scale_estimation` 141 4. `grounded_dimension_reasoning` 142 5. `relative_depth_forward` 143 6. `existence_verification` 144 7. `scale_comparison_size` 145 8. `distance_estimation` 146 9. `relative_position_forward_reasoning` 147 148 Full dataset schema, Q/A JSON layout, and per-file specifications: see the [dataset card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset). 149 150 ### Prepare the data (download → convert) 151 152 **Step 1 — download** from Hugging Face. Each source (`scannet`, `scannetpp`) ships 153 the raw per-frame arrays plus QA JSON and split lists: 154 155 ``` 156 data/scannet/ 157 ├── processed_data//frame__vert.npy # XYZ+RGB points (load_dim=6) 158 │ frame__sp_label.npy # superpoint ids 159 │ frame__part_label.npy # per-point part labels 160 │ frame__object_label.npy # per-point object labels 161 ├── refined_qa_data/{part_qa,object_qa,multiturn_qa}//... 162 └── part_ground3d_{train,val}.txt # scene split lists 163 ``` 164 165 **Step 2 — convert** the raw `.npy` into the flat `.bin` files and the `infos.pkl` 166 the configs actually consume: 167 168 ```bash 169 python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ 170 --root-path data/scannet \ 171 --out-dir data/scannet \ 172 --qa_data_dir data/scannet/refined_qa_data 173 ``` 174 175 **ScanNet++** uses the identical layout — just swap the paths (the converter is dataset-agnostic; 176 the ScanNet++ config reuses `data/scannet/scannet_cls_embedding.pth`): 177 178 ```bash 179 python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ 180 --root-path data/scannetpp \ 181 --out-dir data/scannetpp \ 182 --qa_data_dir data/scannetpp/refined_qa_data 183 ``` 184 185 Resulting layout (what the configs load via `ann_file` + `data_prefix`): 186 187 ``` 188 data/scannet/ 189 ├── points/ super_points/ part_mask/ object_mask/ (_frame_.bin) 190 ├── part3d_glamm_infos_train.pkl 191 ├── part3d_glamm_infos_val.pkl 192 └── scannet_cls_embedding.pth (shipped in this repo) 193 ``` 194 195 > **Joint model only:** the config's `model.decoder.image_dir` expects RGB frames at 196 > `data/scannet/frame_images//.jpg`. These are ScanNet / ScanNet++ images and are 197 > **not redistributable** (so they are not on Hugging Face). Download the raw datasets and extract 198 > the frames each split needs by following **[docs/DATA_IMAGES.md](docs/DATA_IMAGES.md)** 199 > (`tools/build_frame_images.py` does it straight from the `.pkl`). Or use the **3D-only** 200 > checkpoint, which needs no images (`model.decoder.image_dir=None`). 201 202 ## 🤗 Model Zoo 203 204 | Model | Modality | LoRA (r / α) | Eval config | Checkpoint | 205 |---|---|---|---|---| 206 | Ground3D-LMM-4B (Joint) | 3D points + RGB frames | 16 / 32 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint) — main paper result | 207 | Ground3D-LMM-4B (3D-only) | 3D points only | 32 / 64 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}_3d.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D) — no RGB frames required | 208 209 Both checkpoints use **Qwen3-VL-4B** as the LLM backbone (4.47B params, ~400M LoRA-trainable). 210 The two variants have different LoRA ranks, so each ships with its own eval config; the config 211 inheritance keeps the diff between them tiny (`lora_r`, `lora_alpha`, `image_dir`). If you're 212 running through `eval_ground3d.sh`, the launcher probes the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks 213 the matching config automatically — no manual switch needed. 214 215 ## 🏋️ Training 216 217 ### Prepare data 218 1. Download the dataset and arrange under `data/scannet/` and `data/scannetpp/` (see [Local data layout](#local-data-layout)) 219 2. Download pretrained sparse-conv weights into `work_dirs/pretrained/`: 220 - `sstnet_scannet.pth` — used as the point-encoder initialization 221 3. The Qwen3-VL-4B base model will be downloaded automatically by `transformers`. To use a local copy, override via `--cfg-options model.decoder.qwen_model_path=/path/to/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` 222 223 ### Launch training (4 GPUs, LoRA fine-tuning) 224 ```bash 225 bash train.sh 226 ``` 227 228 This launches `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py` on GPUs 0-3 via `torch.distributed.launch`. Checkpoints are saved to `work_dirs/ground3dlmm/epoch_*.pth`. 229 230 ### Customize the training run 231 Common arguments to edit in `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py`: 232 233 | Field | Default | Purpose | 234 |---|---|---| 235 | `model.decoder.qwen_model_path` | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` | Path or HF id of the LLM | 236 | `model.decoder.lora_r`, `lora_alpha` | 16, 32 | LoRA rank and scaling | 237 | `model.decoder.max_point_tokens` | 2000 | Max superpoint tokens fed to LLM | 238 | `train_dataloader.batch_size` | 1 | Per-GPU batch size | 239 | `optim_wrapper.optimizer.lr` | 1e-4 | Base learning rate | 240 | `epoch` | 10 | Total training epochs | 241 | `load_from` | `work_dirs/pretrained/sstnet_scannet.pth` | Backbone init | 242 243 ## 📈 Evaluation 244 245 The paper reports **three categories of metrics**. Full evaluation is a 3-step pipeline: 246 247 ### Step 1 — Run inference (segmentation mIoU + per-scene predictions) 248 249 One launcher, fully argument-driven — pick the dataset / task levels / sub-tasks with flags: 250 ```bash 251 bash eval_ground3d.sh --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # default: scannet, part+object, all sub-tasks 252 253 # choose exactly what to run: 254 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels all # both datasets, part+object+multi_turn 255 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannet --levels part,object --sub_tasks distance_estimation,scale_estimation 256 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannetpp --levels multi_turn 257 bash eval_ground3d.sh --help # full option list (+ --gpus, --out-root, --mask-dump) 258 ``` 259 `--dataset` = `scannet`|`scannetpp`|`all`; `--levels` = any of `part,object,multi_turn` (or `all`); 260 `--sub_tasks` = `all` or a comma list. `--variant` = `joint`|`3d`|`auto` (default `auto`): the launcher 261 inspects the checkpoint's LoRA rank (`r=16` → joint, `r=32` → 3D-only) and picks the matching config, 262 so the Joint and 3D-only weights just work with the same command. Pass `--variant` explicitly to 263 override. The old names `eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp,all}.sh` still work — they're thin wrappers 264 that pass flags through. Outputs: 265 - **Segmentation mIoU** (printed per sub-task) 266 - Per-scene prediction JSONs in `val_outputs_joint/{scannet,scannetpp}/pred_qa_data_val/...` 267 268 > Add `--mask-dump ` to also dump per-QA masks (needed for the **GM-δ** stage below, and used by 269 > the grounding visualization). 270 271 `tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py` runs **two independent stages** — pick what you need via `--stages` 272 (`ape`, `judge`, or `all`). The `--input` dir is searched **recursively**, nested / multi-turn 273 prediction JSONs are flattened automatically, and each sample is tagged with its task. `ape` uses a 274 text LLM (`--llm_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`) to extract numbers; `judge` uses 275 the paper's VL judge (`--judge_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`). Both run via 276 **HuggingFace transformers**. Sanity-check the numeric math with 277 `python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --selftest`. 278 279 ### Step 2 — `ape` : numeric APE + δ@1.25 (the 4 numeric tasks only) 280 ```bash 281 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ 282 --output eval_results/scannet_ape.json --stages ape \ 283 --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 284 ``` 285 Runs **only** on `distance_estimation`, `grounded_dimension_reasoning`, `scale_estimation`, 286 `scale_comparison_size`. The LLM extracts the scalar(s) in metres (per-task JSON shape; a missing 287 prediction → `0.0` so it is penalised), then reports **APE** `|ŝ−s|/s×100%` and **δ@1.25** success 288 (`δ = max(ŝ/s, s/ŝ) ≤ 1.25`; GT==0 pairs skipped; mean over pairs, then macro-averaged per task). 289 290 ### Step 3 — `judge` : LLM judge — Hallucination + Completeness (all tasks) 291 ```bash 292 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ 293 --output eval_results/scannet_judge.json --stages judge \ 294 --judge_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct --gpus 0,1,2,3 295 ``` 296 The Table-4 judge — **Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct** — scores each prediction and reports **Hallucination** 297 and **Completeness** (over all tasks). Run both stages with `--stages all` (the `ape` extractor 298 stays on the text `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`). 299 300 ### Step 3b — `gmdelta` : GM-δ (supplementary, opt-in) 301 GM-δ (Grounded-Measurement) counts a prediction correct only when **mask IoU > 0.3 AND δ ≤ 1.25**, on 302 the numeric tasks that also ground. Run the numeric sub-tasks **with `--mask-dump`** (the mask tree 303 mirrors the prediction tree), then **one command auto-iterates all 4 numeric tasks × both datasets**: 304 ```bash 305 # 1. inference for the 4 numeric tasks on both datasets, dumping per-QA masks 306 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels part \ 307 --sub_tasks distance_estimation,grounded_dimension_reasoning,scale_estimation,scale_comparison_size \ 308 --mask-dump masks --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth 309 310 # 2. GM-δ across all of them in a single run 311 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta \ 312 --input val_outputs_joint --mask_dump_dir masks \ 313 --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 --output eval_results/gmdelta.json 314 ``` 315 It reports GM-δ **per (dataset, task)** and **overall**. `--gmdelta_task all` (default) auto-discovers 316 the numeric tasks; pass a single task name to restrict. 317 318 ### Metric provenance (the paper's metrics) 319 320 | Metric | Provided by | Tasks | 321 |---|---|---| 322 | Segmentation mIoU | `tools/test.py` → `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` | all sub-tasks (over each QA's `` grounding) | 323 | APE & δ@1.25 (LLM-extracted) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages ape` | 4 numeric tasks | 324 | Hallucination + Completeness (LLM judge) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages judge` | all tasks | 325 | GM-δ (IoU>0.3 ∧ δ≤1.25), *supplementary* | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta` | grounded-measurement | 326 327 > mIoU is computed per `(level, sub-task)` over the QAs that emit a `` grounding. Core writer: 364 `uniseg3d/grounding_viz.py`. For multi-turn dialogues (`task_level=multi_turn_qa_data`) each grounding 365 turn contributes one region, so a cross-object conversation produces one red object and one green 366 object in a single `.ply`. 367 368 ## 🛠️ Repository structure 369 370 ``` 371 Ground3D-LMM/ 372 ├── configs/ 373 │ ├── ground3dlmm_train.py 374 │ ├── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py 375 │ └── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannetpp.py 376 ├── data/ (user-populated; see Local data layout) 377 ├── docs/ 378 │ └── INSTALL.md 379 ├── tools/ 380 │ ├── train.py, test.py 381 │ ├── dist_train.sh, dist_test.sh 382 │ ├── create_data.py 383 │ └── evaluate_text_metrics.py 384 ├── uniseg3d/ (model + transforms + criteria) 385 │ ├── uniseg3d.py Grounded_LMM_main (entry point) 386 │ ├── query_decoder.py Grounded_Decoder_Joint / _Eval 387 │ ├── spconv_unet.py point encoder 388 │ ├── point_qwen3_vl.py Qwen3-VL with point-embedding injection 389 │ ├── transforms_3d.py QA_Generation_v2 / _Test 390 │ ├── unified_metric.py Part3DGlamm_SegMetric 391 │ └── ... 392 ├── work_dirs/ (checkpoints + logs, gitignored) 393 ├── train.sh one-line training launcher 394 ├── eval_ground3d_scannet.sh eval on ScanNet 395 ├── eval_ground3d_scannetpp.sh eval on ScanNet++ 396 ├── eval_ground3d_all.sh eval on both 397 ├── environment.yml conda spec (pinned versions) 398 ├── pyproject.toml 399 └── LICENSE Apache-2.0 400 ``` 401 402 ## 🙏 Acknowledgments 403 404 This codebase builds upon several open-source projects: 405 406 - from turtle import pd
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import spconv.pytorch as spconv
from torch_scatter import scatter_mean
import MinkowskiEngine as ME

from mmdet3d.registry import MODELS
from mmdet3d.structures import PointData
from mmdet3d.models import Base3DDetector
from .mask_matrix_nms import mask_matrix_nms

from mmdet3d.registry import TASK_UTILS
from .structures import InstanceData_

import copy


class UniSeg3DMixin:
    def point_prompt_predict_by_feat(self, out, superpoints, point_prompt_instances):
        if out['masks'][0] == None:
            obj_gt = torch.as_tensor([])
            obj_res = torch.as_tensor([])
        else:
            obj_res = self.point_prompt_predict_by_feat_object(out, superpoints)
            obj_gt = point_prompt_instances[0].sp_masks[:,superpoints]

        return [
            PointData(
                point_prompt_object_pred_masks=obj_res.cpu().numpy(),
                point_prompt_object_gt_masks=obj_gt.cpu().numpy())]

    def point_prompt_predict_by_feat_object(self, out, superpoints):
        mask_pred = out['masks'][0]
        mask_pred_sigmoid = mask_pred.sigmoid()
        mask_pred_sigmoid = mask_pred_sigmoid[:, superpoints]
        mask_pred = mask_pred_sigmoid > self.test_cfg.sp_score_thr
        
        return mask_pred

- OpenMMLab 官方为常见 torch×cuda 组合提供预编译 wheel，但 torch 2.4.1+cu118 不在其中 → pip 只能源码编译。
- 源码编译需要：本机 CUDA 工具链（CUDA_HOME 指向 nvcc）、正确的 setuptools（旧版，因为编译脚本用 pkg_resources）、禁用 build isolation（让编译进程看到环境里已装好的 torch 和旧 setuptools）。
- build isolation 解释：pip 默认在隔离的临时环境里构建，那个环境只有 pyproject 声明的 build 依赖（最新 setuptools），看不到已装的 torch → mmcv 的 setup.py 需要在编译期 import torch 来确定 CUDA 版本 → 必须 --no-build-isolation。

MinkowskiEngine 编译解释：
- NVIDIA 的通用稀疏卷积库（用于高维稀疏张量）。
- 本项目用它做批组装与坐标量化（ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate / ME.TensorField）→ uniseg3d.py:399-415。
- v0.5.4 tag 与 torch 2.4 的 CUDA 模板不兼容 → 用 master 分支（02fc608）。
- 需要 OpenBLAS 头文件；系统 libopenblas-dev 优于 conda-forge openblas-devel（libgfortran.so.3 运行时错误）。
- MAX_JOBS=8 控制并行编译防 OOM。

spconv：直接用预编译 wheel（spconv-cu118），注意 GPU 架构（sm_90 H100 需要 cu120）。
torch-scatter：PyG 的 wheel 索引 -f。

LLM stack：transformers==4.57.6（Qwen3-VL 需要 ≥4.45）、peft==0.18.1（LoRA）。
源码证据：query_decoder.py:11-13。

未文档化依赖：qwen_vl_utils（query_decoder.py:23）、hydra、nncore（point_qwen3_vl.py:7-9）。这三个不在 environment.yml / INSTALL.md / pyproject.toml 中（我 grep 过 yml/toml/md 无匹配）。所以 `import uniseg3d` 可能失败——待本地验证（也许 pip 解析间接装上了，比如 hydra 可能不是任何列出包的依赖；qwen-vl-utils 不是 transformers 的强制依赖）。讲义中作为「排查思路」：用 `python -c "import uniseg3d"` 验证 + 逐个补装。这是有真实证据支撑的教学点。

好，还有一个问题：uniseg3d/__init__.py 没有导入 point_qwen3_vl 模块本身，但 query_decoder.py（在 __init__.py 第 3 行被导入）顶部导入了 point_qwen3_vl 和 qwen_vl_utils。而 point_qwen3_vl.py 顶部导入 hydra/nncore。所以 import 链是：
`import uniseg3d` → `__init__.py:3 from .query_decoder import ...` → `query_decoder.py:20 from .point_qwen3_vl import ...` + `query_decoder.py:23 from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info` → `point_qwen3_vl.py:7-9 from hydra import compose; from nncore.nn import ...`

同时 `__init__.py:1 from .uniseg3d import UniSeg3D` → uniseg3d.py:5-7 spconv/torch_scatter/ME。

所以 import uniseg3d 需要全部就位。这个链在讲义 4.4 里画出来。

关于 `pd` from turtle：不提。

pyproject 的 packages = ["uniseg3d"] 说明 editable install 只装 uniseg3d 包；tools/、configs/ 不安装，所以要 PYTHONPATH=. 运行 tools/test.py（README 用 PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py）——其实 editable install 后 tools 不是包，运行 tools/test.py 时 python 会把 tools 目录加入 sys.path，而 configs 是通过相对路径读取的。PYTHONPATH=. 主要是为了让 `import uniseg3d` … 等等，pip install -e . 之后 uniseg3d 已经可导入，为什么 README 还要 PYTHONPATH=.？因为 mmengine Config.fromfile 需要从 repo 根相对路径读 config，以及 custom_imports？其实 tools/test.py 里应该有 import。这个细节属于 u1-l4 的内容，本讲一句带过即可：仓库的入口脚本是 tools/*.py，安装本包后它们不需要安装，直接在仓库根目录运行。

# 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清楚 Ground3D-LMM 的依赖为什么「难装」：它同时依赖 OpenMMLab 栈（mmengine/mmcv/mmdet/mmdet3d）、两个稀疏卷积库（spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine）和一套 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），而这些包的 CUDA 产物必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 版本、GPU 架构三方对齐。
2. 按 `docs/INSTALL.md` 的 **Option B** 手动完成环境搭建，尤其是两处源码编译：`mmcv==2.1.0`（`--no-build-isolation`）与 MinkowskiEngine（master 分支）。
3. 理解 `environment.yml` 为什么「刻意不完整」、`pyproject.toml` 为什么只声明极少的依赖。
4. 用仓库自带的验证脚本和 `import uniseg3d` 检查安装是否真正可用，并掌握「顺着 import 报错补依赖」的排查方法。

本讲**不涉及任何模型代码逻辑**——那是第 3、4 单元的事。我们只解决一件事：把环境装到能让 `import uniseg3d` 成功为止。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲是整套手册里最「运维味」的一讲，需要先了解几个基础概念：

- **conda 环境**：一个独立的 Python 解释器 + 包集合的沙盒。3D 深度学习项目的依赖版本冲突频繁，永远不要往 base 环境里装。
- **wheel 与源码编译**：`pip install xxx` 时，pip 优先下载预编译好的二进制包（wheel）；如果没有匹配的 wheel，pip 会下载源码（sdist），在你机器上现场编译。编译型扩展（含 CUDA 算子的包）要求本机有编译工具链（gcc、nvcc）。
- **CUDA 三方对齐**：一个含 CUDA 算子的包能否工作，取决于三个维度同时匹配——PyTorch 编译时用的 CUDA 版本（如 `2.4.1+cu118`）、本机安装的 CUDA 工具链（`CUDA_HOME` 指向的地方）、GPU 的计算架构（compute capability，如 A100 是 sm_80、H100 是 sm_90）。任何一环错位，轻则编译失败，重则编译成功但运行时报 `no kernel image is available`。
- **build isolation（构建隔离）**：pip 默认在临时目录里新建一个隔离环境来构建源码包，那个环境里只有 `pyproject.toml` 声明的构建依赖，**看不到你已装好的 torch**。凡是 `setup.py` 里需要在编译期 `import torch` 的包（mmcv 就是），都必须加 `--no-build-isolation` 关掉隔离。
- **OpenMMLab 栈**：mmengine（训练引擎与注册表）→ mmcv（底层算子与视觉工具）→ mmdet（2D 检测）→ mmdet3d（3D 检测/分割）。上一讲说过，Ground3D-LMM 的模型类全部注册在 mmdet3d 的 registry 里，所以这四层缺一不可。
- **稀疏卷积**：室内点云在体素化后绝大多数体素是空的，稀疏卷积只对非空体素做计算。本项目用到**两个**稀疏卷积库：spconv（跑 SpConvUNet 主干）和 MinkowskiEngine（做批组装与坐标量化，见 4.3 节）。
- **peft / LoRA**：LoRA 是只训练少量低秩矩阵的微调方法，peft 是它的官方实现库。安装上只需一个 `pip install peft`，但版本要与 transformers 配套。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| [docs/INSTALL.md](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/docs/INSTALL.md) | 安装主文档：测试环境表、Option A/B 两条安装路径、验证脚本、smoke test、常见报错 |
| [environment.yml](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/environment.yml) | conda 依赖清单（版本锁定），**刻意不包含** mmcv/mmdet/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine |
| [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/pyproject.toml) | 本仓库自身的 pip 包元数据，只声明纯 Python 依赖 |
| [README.md](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/README.md) | Install 段落给出了「environment.yml 不能独立完成安装」的明确警告 |
| [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py) | 模型主文件，顶部 import 了 spconv / torch_scatter / MinkowskiEngine——这三个依赖「装不上就全盘 import 失败」的源头 |
| [uniseg3d/query_decoder.py](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py) | 解码器，顶部 import transformers / peft / qwen_vl_utils |
| [uniseg3d/point_qwen3_vl.py](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/point_qwen3_vl.py) | Qwen3-VL 注入点云 token 的实现，顶部 import hydra / nncore |
| [uniseg3d/\_\_init\_\_.py](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/__init__.py) | 包入口，`import uniseg3d` 时的 import 链起点 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲的四个最小模块：**4.1 conda 环境与依赖清单**、**4.2 mmcv 源码编译**、**4.3 MinkowskiEngine 源码编译**、**4.4 本包安装与依赖验证**。

### 4.1 conda 环境与依赖清单

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

Ground3D-LMM 官方锁定的测试环境是：Ubuntu 20.04/22.04、Python 3.10、CUDA 11.8、PyTorch 2.4.1、A100 80GB 或 RTX 3090 24GB：

| 组件 | 版本 | 来源 |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Ubuntu 20.04 / 22.04 | [docs/INSTALL.md:L5-L15](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/docs/INSTALL.md#L5-L15) 的测试环境表 |
| Python | 3.10 | 同上 |
| CUDA | 11.8 | 同上 |
| PyTorch | 2.4.1 | 同上 |

仓库给了两条安装路径（[docs/INSTALL.md:L17-L27](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/docs/INSTALL.md#L17-L27)）：

- **Option A**：`conda env create -f environment.yml` 一步到位（推荐先试）；
- **Option B**：手动逐步安装——**如果 Option A 在某个 OpenMMLab 包上失败，回退到 Option B**。

关键认知：**Option A 并不能独立装完**。这不是缺陷，而是刻意设计——README 里有一段明确的警告：

> **Heads-up:** `conda env create -f environment.yml` does **not** fully work on its own —— 见 [README.md:L52-L56](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/README.md#L52-L56)

原因在 4.2/4.3 展开：`mmcv==2.1.0` 没有对应 torch 2.4.1 的预编译 wheel，MinkowskiEngine 必须从特定分支源码编译，而这两步需要交互式的环境变量设置，conda 清单表达不了。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

Option A + 补装的整体流程：

```text
conda env create -f environment.yml     # 装：python3.10 + torch2.4.1+cu118 + mmengine
        │                                #     + spconv + torch-scatter + LLM栈 + 科学计算库
        ▼
（若失败 → 改走 Option B 手动逐步装，见 4.2）
        ▼
补装源码编译三件：mmcv → mmdet → mmdet3d → MinkowskiEngine   ← environment.yml 刻意不管的部分
        ▼
pip install -e .                        # 安装本仓库的 uniseg3d 包
        ▼
跑验证脚本 + import uniseg3d            # 见 4.4
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看 `environment.yml` 的开头——构建工具被刻意钉在最前面：

[environment.yml:L1-L14](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/environment.yml#L1-L14) 声明了环境名 `ground3d`、三个 channel，并在 pip 依赖列表的**第一组**就安装 `setuptools<70`、`wheel`、`ninja`。注释写明原因：mmcv/MinkowskiEngine 的源码编译在较新 setuptools 上会报 `No module named 'pkg_resources'`，所以必须先把旧版 setuptools 钉进环境。

接着是 PyTorch 与 mmengine（[environment.yml:L16-L23](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/environment.yml#L16-L23)）：torch/vision/audio 三个包都用 `+cu118` 后缀，并通过 `--extra-index-url` 指向 PyTorch 官方的 CUDA 11.8 wheel 源；mmengine 钉在 `0.10.7`。

然后是整个文件最重要的一段注释（[environment.yml:L25-L29](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/environment.yml#L25-L29)）：**mmcv / mmdet / mmdet3d 被刻意不写进清单**，因为 mmcv 2.1.0 对 torch 2.4.1 没有预编译 wheel、必须用 `--no-build-isolation` 源码编译，MinkowskiEngine 0.5.4 也是源码构建，清单完成后还要按 `docs/INSTALL.md` 的步骤 3、4、4b 手动补装。
